text:
Toronto traded Matthew Knies to Columbus for Kirill Marchenko in late September and signed him to a six-year, $75 million extension. For 14 games the bet looked smart: 14 points, eight on the power play, and a hat trick against Buffalo on Oct 15.

Then he left the Oct 26 game in Calgary after seven minutes and hasn't played since. The Hockey News reported on Nov 16 that he was skating in full team gear for the first time, with Toronto stuck in a six-game slide (Toronto Hockey Daily), though Hockey Patrol called the return timeline update "sobering."

What he gave them before the injury was mostly real. At five on five the Leafs took 56.1% of expected goals with him on, about 11 points better than without, and his six goals came on 4.7 expected, a little hot but nothing wild. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at the 90th percentile among forwards in chances from the home-plate area last season.

The worry Evolving-Hockey raised last season was the other end: he faced top competition and gave up more chances than most forwards.

What to watch: when he returns, whether the power-play role is still his.
headline: Marchenko's Leafs start, on hold
